template.name: weekly_one_on_one
template.description: Weekly 1:1 between a manager and direct report to review work, surface blockers early, check well-being, and maintain momentum on growth and priorities.

sections.label: Current Focus and Progress
sections.description: Capture the top active work items since the last 1:1, what moved, key outcomes, and current status against 'done' definitions.

sections.label: Upcoming Priorities and Plans
sections.description: Record the few most important tasks until the next 1:1, why they matter, expected effort, and planned milestones.

sections.label: Risks and Blockers
sections.description: List concrete obstacles or dependencies slowing work, what is needed to unblock, owner of the unblock, and urgency.

sections.label: Support Requests and Commits
sections.description: Track specific asks of the manager and any commitments from either party with owners and due dates.

sections.label: Feedback and Guidance
sections.description: Log coaching, decisions, or quality-bar guidance the manager provides to adjust approach, scope, or priorities.

sections.label: Well-being and Engagement
sections.description: Note how the report is feeling, workload sustainability, morale, and environmental factors affecting effectiveness.

sections.label: Recognition and Wins
sections.description: Call out notable achievements, shipped outcomes, or positive behaviors to reinforce.

sections.label: Career Growth and Development
sections.description: Document growth topics such as skills to build, role aspirations, stretch opportunities, learning plans, and check-ins on development goals.

sections.label: Other
sections.description: Anything material that doesn't fit a declared section. Prefer declared sections; use this only when nothing else fits.

phases.label: Rapport and Check-in
phases.goal: Build rapport and understand how the report is doing personally and professionally to set context for the rest of the meeting.

phases.label: Work Review and Blockers
phases.goal: Get crisp visibility into current work and surface risks early.

phases.label: Planning and Alignment
phases.goal: Align on next-week priorities, capture requests, and provide guidance to ensure momentum.

phases.label: Growth and Wrap
phases.goal: Spend time on development if needed and confirm owners, dates, and takeaways before closing.

issues.description: No explicit review loop for prior action items/commitments, despite the user wanting “enough structure that nothing important gets dropped.” While `support_requests_and_commits` captures new asks, nothing in sections or phases prompts checking carryover items from the last 1:1.
issues.suggested_fix: Amend `support_requests_and_commits` description to begin with “Review status of open commitments from prior 1:1s, mark done/blocked/rolled,” and add `support_requests_and_commits` to the `work_review` phase’s `sections_in_focus` so the status check happens before planning. Optionally note that unresolved items should spawn updates in `risks_and_blockers` or be re-committed.

issues.description: Overlap between `risks_and_blockers` (which asks for “what is needed to unblock, owner of the unblock, and urgency”) and `support_requests_and_commits` (which also tracks asks, owners, and due dates) may cause double-entry or mis-bucketing.
issues.suggested_fix: Narrow `risks_and_blockers` to context, root cause, impact, and risk level. Move owners/dates/requests to `support_requests_and_commits`. Add a note in `risks_and_blockers`: “Any resulting asks/commitments should be captured in `support_requests_and_commits`.”

issues.description: `feedback_and_guidance` is framed one‑way (manager → report). For a conversational 1:1, upward feedback and questions from the report are important.
issues.suggested_fix: Broaden `feedback_and_guidance` to “bidirectional feedback and coaching (report ↔ manager), decisions, and quality-bar guidance,” or rename to `feedback_coaching_and_decisions` with the updated description.

missing_aspects: Explicit review of carryover action items/commitments from the previous 1:1
Space that explicitly invites report-led topics/questions to keep the tone conversational
Two-way (upward) feedback from the report to the manager
critique.rationale: Overall the template is strong: sections are substantive and well-named, phases and pacing are sensible, and the content aligns with a weekly 1:1. The main gap is the lack of an explicit review of prior commitments, which risks dropping items—contrary to the user’s stated goal. Minor clarifications will reduce overlap and encourage a more conversational, two-way dynamic.
critique.next_iteration_focus: Add an explicit prior-commitments review by updating `support_requests_and_commits` and including it early (e.g., in `work_review`).

sections.label: Check-in and Report-led Topics
sections.description: Note how the report is feeling, workload sustainability, morale or team dynamics, and any report-led agenda items or questions they want to discuss that do not fit elsewhere.

sections.label: Recognition and Wins
sections.description: Call out notable achievements, shipped outcomes, or positive behaviors to reinforce.

sections.label: Career Growth and Development
sections.description: Document growth topics such as skills to build, role aspirations, stretch opportunities, learning plans, and check-ins on development goals.

sections.label: Other
sections.description: Anything material that doesn't fit a declared section. Prefer declared sections; use this only when nothing else fits.

phases.label: Rapport and Check-in
phases.goal: Build rapport and understand how the report is doing personally and professionally to set context for the rest of the meeting.

phases.label: Work Review and Blockers
phases.goal: Get crisp visibility into current work, review prior commitments, and surface risks early.

phases.label: Planning and Alignment
phases.goal: Align on next-week priorities, capture requests, and provide guidance to ensure momentum.

phases.label: Growth and Wrap
phases.goal: Spend time on development if needed and confirm owners, dates, and takeaways before closing.

issues.description: Template manually includes a section with id `other`, but the system auto-appends an "Other" section. This risks duplicate/conflicting sections (and potentially a duplicate id), creating ambiguity and structural breakage.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the explicit `other` section from `sections`. Treat `check_in_and_report_topics` as the catch-all for report-led/misc items that don't fit elsewhere.

issues.description: Section id `support_requests_and_commits` doesn't match the label "Support Requests and Commitments" and could be confused with version-control "commits."
issues.suggested_fix: Rename the id to `support_requests_and_commitments` to align with the label and avoid ambiguity.

issues.description: `current_focus_and_progress` language leans toward a status-report tone (e.g., "status against 'done' definitions"), which conflicts with the user's desire for a conversational feel.
issues.suggested_fix: Soften the description to emphasize discussion and learning (e.g., "Top active work since last 1:1, what moved, outcomes, what's still in progress, and notable learnings—briefly, not a full status report.")

issues.description: Potential mis-bucketing between `feedback_coaching_and_decisions` and `support_requests_and_commits` for decisions vs. resulting actions.
issues.suggested_fix: In `feedback_coaching_and_decisions`, explicitly say: "Log decisions and brief rationale here; any resulting action items/owners/dates go in `support_requests_and_commitments`." Keep `support_requests_and_commitments` focused on actionable follow-ups only.

issues.description: Growth is intended "every few weeks"; a fixed 15% every week might reduce time for work topics when growth isn’t on the agenda.
issues.suggested_fix: Note in the `growth_and_wrap` phase goal that the time is optional and can be reallocated to work review/planning when no growth topics are queued.

critique.rationale: Well-structured, comprehensive, and well-paced for a weekly 1:1, with clear coverage of work, blockers, rapport, and development. The main flaw is the explicit `other` section, which will duplicate the auto-appended one and cause confusion. Minor wording and naming tweaks would better match the conversational intent and reduce mis-bucketing risk.
critique.next_iteration_focus: Remove the explicit `other` section to avoid duplication with the auto-appended one.

issues.description: Section id `other` is explicitly included even though an `other` catch‑all is typically auto‑appended; using the same id could cause duplication or conflicts.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the explicit `other` section. Rely on the platform’s auto‑appended catch‑all, or, if you truly need a custom catch‑all, give it a distinct id (e.g., `parking_lot`) and clarify when to use it versus the auto one.

issues.description: The id `check_in_and_report_topics` can be misread as “status report topics” rather than “direct report–led topics.”
issues.suggested_fix: Rename the id to `check_in_and_direct_report_topics` (label can stay the same or become “Check‑in and DR‑led Topics”) to avoid ambiguity for filers.

issues.description: Work-focused phases consume 70% of time (0.35 + 0.35). For a conversation‑oriented 1:1, this may skew toward status unless participants are disciplined.
issues.suggested_fix: Consider rebalancing to 0.30 (work_review), 0.30 (planning_alignment), 0.20 (rapport_check_in), 0.20 (growth_and_wrap), or note guidance that progress updates should be very brief to protect conversational time.

critique.rationale: Well-structured, with 8 substantive, clearly distinguished sections that map to the user’s goals (work visibility, well‑being, blockers, and periodic growth). Phases are coherent, reference valid sections, and sum to 1.0. Only minor polish items remain around the explicit ‘other’ section, a small naming ambiguity, and optional pacing tweak to further emphasize conversation over status.
